title: Sightseeing in London and Copenhagen and Danish habits
summary: A London prize fight, Madame Tussauds and churches, and a Copenhagen tour of cooperative housing and orderly queues.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: New York. Yeah, I went to a prize fight over there. I saw Cooper in London. I saw them fight for the English heavyweight title. And they had some celebrities there. They had Bassett, the boy that fought last night. He was there. They introduced him, Norris, and this man that promoted the fight. I just remember his name, promoted the fight last night from California. He was there. And several other fighters. And the fighter who I wanted to see from Sweden was fighting Patterson. He was there and introduced him.
You didn't see him fight, though?

No, they just introduced him. And two or three days afterwards or so he was to fight Patterson. They had a plane of paper. Then I went and saw Madame Tussauds at Wax Museum. And they had a lady, her husband was a piano player. He was a piano player. His name is Graham. And his wife is named Molly. You know people. And she had taken me to all these places and she could explain the whole history of these things. I went to the Westminster. I went to St. Paul's Cathedral. And inside these churches they have different historical backgrounds. And she could explain all these things to me. It really was an enjoyable trip. I liked that. And then when we got to Sweden, to Denmark, they had a young man. He asked me had I been around. And I told him, no, I hadn't saw very much which places I had walked downtown. So he told me, he said, well, one day I'm going to come and get you. He said, well, it's available and I'm going to take you around. So I said, well, anytime it's convenient with you. So he said, well, I'll pick you up in about three days. He said, it was on a Tuesday. He said, I'll take you around. And I was supposed to go to Henrik's house to dinner. And so he said, well, I'll take you around and then I'll bring you to Henrik's. Henrik's knew him. And so sure enough he came, like he said, 12th day. And he brought me all over Copenhagen. And he showed me all the interesting things there. He brought me by this hospital where the, I think where there's Lisbon's, where they changed men into women. Oh yeah, I remember. And he brought me to this hospital and he brought me to this modern projects they have there. They have projects there, real modern projects. And he showed me those. Now there's one thing he was telling me that amazed me about these projects. One was 11 stewards. And he told me that 100 families got together and they built this. Not only one, they got several of them. There's seven of them. And they built that together and they moved in there. See these 100 families. And anything that these 100 families don't use, they rent it. See, so they bind this project together, 100 families. And I said, well that's really amazing, I say, that 100 families could buy a building like that and get along and live in it, you know. And it seems like it's very peaceful for what he told me, that they never have any incidents of any kind. And there's another thing that I wish that people throughout America could adopt this system. Now they got a system there like getting on streetcars. I don't care how, like if you're standing in a line, they got a line, they stand at this particular point. And I don't care how far a line is back when you see somebody coming up. They never try to get in front or nothing. They go back behind that line and they don't have no police there to make a way. And it'd be snowing or raining. And they all stand there and wait until their turn comes to get in those cars. Now sometimes it'd be three and four, five cars before the fellow behind the line can get in the car and he waits. And nobody pushes or nobody comes. See, like we, the people here got the system, they run and if you're waiting for the streetcar, they allow it to jump in front. You know, just come and jump right on in front. They never do that or no pushing or nothing. And I watched that in all those countries. And I used to stand them.
